title: Reliable sampling-based RKHS norm estimation via superconvergence
summary: Kernel methods are one of the cornerstones of learning-based control, modern system identification, surrogate modelling, and related fields. A key advantage of this class of learning and function approximation methods is the availability of quantitative error bounds, which in turn play a key role in guaranteeing the safety of learned controllers and related learning-based algorithms. However, these error bounds rely on a particular property of the target function -- its reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) norm -- which is usually impossible to obtain in practice.
